AQUA_REGION.description: Optional Aqua SaaS region selector (us | eu | apac | singapore). Resolves to a per-region endpoint: us / default / empty -> https://cloudsploit.com; eu -> https://eu.cloudsploit.com; apac (alias: ap) -> https://apac.cloudsploit.com; singapore (alias: sg) -> https://singapore.cloudsploit.com. Unrecognised tokens log a warning and fall back to the US default. AQUA_HOST is intentionally NOT exposed as an environment variable for the SaaS variant — the host is hardcoded so an operator can't accidentally point at the wrong tenant URL.

AQUA_REGISTRY.description: Optional Aqua SaaS registry name to scope the vulnerability search to (forwarded as the registry_name query parameter in the GET /api/v2/risks/vulnerabilities request). Registries are how Aqua organises image sources (ECR / GCR / ACR / Docker Hub / Harbor / Quay / Artifactory); leaving this blank queries across every registry the service account can see.

AQUA_REPO.description: Optional Aqua SaaS repository / image name to scope the vulnerability search to (forwarded as the image_name query parameter in the GET /api/v2/risks/vulnerabilities request). Useful when a tenant has thousands of images and the operator only wants findings for a specific image. Leave blank to query every image in the selected registry (or every registry if AQUA_REGISTRY is also blank).

AQUA_MIN_SEVERITY.description: Optional minimum severity floor (info | low | medium | high | critical). Forwarded to Aqua SaaS as the severity query parameter on GET /api/v2/risks/vulnerabilities (so the tenant only paginates results that survive the floor) AND enforced client-side after Faraday severity normalisation (handles Aqua's critical/high/medium/low/negligible enum and CVSS base-score fallback). Defaults to info (no filtering).

name: aqua_saas
title: Aqua SaaS (CNAPP)
description: Aqua SaaS (CloudSploit / Aqua Wave) Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform (CNAPP / CSPM) REST importer. Thin wrapper around the aqua_enterprise executor that hardcodes the tenant URL to Aqua's hosted SaaS edition (https://cloudsploit.com by default, with an optional AQUA_REGION arg that picks a per-region endpoint — us | eu | apac | singapore); every helper (auth, pagination, severity / status normalisation, CVE / CWE harvesting, host bucketing, Faraday vulnerability shape) is reused verbatim from aqua_enterprise so the two stay in lockstep. Pulls cloud-security vulnerability findings via the canonical GET /api/v2/risks/vulnerabilities endpoint and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON to stdout. /api/v2/risks/vulnerabilities is paginated via page + pagesize cursor (with count / total honoured for early-stop, length-of-chunk fallback, dedup via vulnerability_id + package + image_id) and filters on registry_name / image_name / severity; /api/v2/images is optionally consulted to enrich the finding payload with os / digest / labels / base_image metadata. Each Aqua image (registry + repository + image_id) becomes one Faraday host (synthetic 0.0.0.0 ip because CNAPP findings live on container images, not on IPs) with hostnames = {registry}/{repository}:{tag}@{image_id}; per-image findings attached as Faraday vulnerabilities — one per Aqua finding id with [CNAPP] engine prefix, '{vulnId} in {package}@{version} on {registry}/{repo}:{tag}' in the title, description / vuln_id / package / image / registry / repository / image_id / image_tag / os / architecture / base_image / scan_date / fix_version / first_seen / last_seen / status / severity / fix_available / exploitability / score / vector in the description; solution / remediation / recommendation / 'Upgrade {package} to {fix_version}.' fallback surfaces as Faraday resolution. Refs include CWE-* (single + list + list-of-dict shapes with the CWE- prefix collapsed, deduped across finding + image), 'Aqua-Vuln: {vulnId}' pivot label, finding.nvd_url / vendor_url / url / advisoryUrl, and references / links / external_references URL shapes (string + dict with href / url) from finding + image. CVE list harvested via a strict CVE-\d{4}-\d+ regex from finding.name / vulnerability / vulnerability_id / title / description / summary (token-scan over free-form strings) + cve / cveId / cve_id / cves / aliases (string + list-of-string + list-of-dict shapes); deduped case-insensitively, malformed strings like 'CVE-2024-aaaa' rejected. Severity normalised from Aqua's string enum (critical / high / medium / low / negligible — also accepts Important / Major / Moderate / Minor / Information / None / Unspecified / Trivial / Unknown) with CVSS v3 / v2 base-score bucketing as a fallback when only a numeric aqua_score / cvss_score / score / nvd_score is given (≤0/>10 → info, <4 low, <7 medium, <9 high, ≥9 critical); AQUA_MIN_SEVERITY both forwarded to Aqua as the severity filter (when above info) AND enforced client-side after normalisation. Status mapped from finding.status / ack_status / vuln_status (open / new / active / detected / reopened / in_progress → open, fixed / resolved / closed / mitigated / remediated / patched → closed, suppressed / muted / ignored / dismissed / wont_fix / risk_accepted / acknowledged / false_positive / expired → risk-accepted). Auth: Aqua SaaS uses a local-account username / password pair (or SAML / SSO-federated identity routed through the tenant login). The pair is sent as JSON to POST /api/v1/login; the response carries a short-lived bearer token (tolerated bare or wrapped under data / data[0]) that is then sent as Authorization: Bearer <token> on subsequent calls. AQUA_HOST is intentionally NOT exposed as an env var — the host is hardcoded to https://cloudsploit.com (with an optional AQUA_REGION arg that picks a per-region URL); the self-hosted / on-prem flavour is handled separately by the aqua_enterprise executor. Tag namespace = aqua_saas so Faraday workspaces can distinguish ingest provenance from the aqua_enterprise executor.
